# OTPKeep v0.2.1 — Lighter in the menu bar, and a code from any script

Released on `2026-10-28`.

> OTPKeep is a free, private authenticator for TOTP, HOTP and Steam codes that lives in your menu bar: a click, a
> shortcut or a few typed letters give you the code, and your accounts never leave your own devices.

## Summary

This release makes OTPKeep a quieter resident of your menu bar. The icon now opens the system's own menu with your
accounts and their codes, no web page runs while OTPKeep rests there, and open windows use far less CPU. Scripts
can ask the running app for a code, and many fixes make unlocking, sync, the clipboard and saving more dependable.
It runs on macOS and Linux.

## Who this release is for

You keep OTPKeep running all day and reach for a code many times, sometimes from a script or a terminal, and you
want the app that waits in your menu bar to cost you nothing until you need it.

If you have ever:

- run `otpkeep code` while the app was open and waited five seconds for a `BUSY` error
- noticed an always-on app holding memory or CPU while you were not using it
- clicked a menu bar icon and waited for a panel to draw, when all you wanted was one code
- unlocked with your master password and seen a browser helper start for a password box

then v0.2.1 gives you the code from a plain system menu or straight from your script, and stays out of the way the
rest of the time.

## Before you upgrade

- The quick panel and its **Menu bar panel opacity** setting are gone: the menu bar icon now opens a menu (see
  below). Nothing else changes — your accounts, settings, shortcuts and pairings carry over as they are.

## What you can do now

**Pick a code from the menu bar menu.** Click the icon: your most recently used accounts come first, each with its
current code, its name and its own shortcut. Choose one and the code is on the clipboard; everything else is under
**More accounts**.

**Get a code from a script while the app runs.** `otpkeep code github` now asks the running app instead of failing
with `BUSY`. You decide whether scripts may do this with **Allow scripts to get codes from the running app** — on
by default without a master password, off until you turn it on with one. See
[Using OTPKeep from scripts](https://github.com/weikxs/otpkeep/blob/v0.2.1/docs/scripting.md).

**Unlock with the system's own dialog.** With a master password, choose **Unlock…** in the menu. On macOS the
system's password dialog asks, so no web page starts just to unlock.

**Leave it running.** While OTPKeep rests in the menu bar no web page runs; the search panel and the main window are
made when you ask for them and let go 30 seconds after you close them.

**Recover when something is busy or damaged.** If another OTPKeep, the keychain or the disk holds up your data, the
windows offer **Try again**; a damaged vault file can be put back to its previous version, and the damaged file is
kept.

## What's new

### The menu bar

- **A native menu instead of the quick panel.** **Search…**, then 30 accounts (10–50, a new setting), the most
  recently used first, then **More accounts (N)**, **Open OTPKeep**, **Manage in the browser…**, **Sync…**,
  **Settings…** and **Quit OTPKeep**. The codes are brought up to date when they change and when the pointer
  reaches the icon. The recently used list is remembered on this device only and never synced.
- **Unlock from the menu.** On macOS with the system's password dialog; on Linux with a small password window that
  closes once the data is open. A shortcut pressed before the password was entered asks the same way.
- **Counter-based (HOTP) accounts** make a new code only when you choose them in the menu.

### Scripts and the command line

- **`otpkeep code` works while the app runs** (macOS, Linux), through a private local socket in the data folder.
  When scripts are not allowed it answers `DISABLED` (exit code 12). Codes given to scripts do not count as
  recently used.

### Lighter and steadier

- **Far less CPU in open windows.** Countdowns update once a second and the rings empty by themselves; long lists
  draw only the accounts on screen.
- **Almost nothing while hidden.** Countdowns run only in a window on screen, and catch up when it is shown.
- **No frozen windows** while the master password is checked, a backup is encrypted, or pictures and backups are
  imported; searching and changing many accounts at once are faster in large vaults.
- **A small problem log.** Warnings and errors are kept in a log file of at most 1 MB plus one older file, to help
  with problem reports. It never holds secrets, codes or account names.

## Bug fixes

- macOS: unlocking with a master password no longer leaves about 64 MB of extra memory held for minutes.
- An imported name like `Example Cloud:ops@example.com` is saved as `Example Cloud`, so the account is no longer
  shown twice; accounts already saved are shown the same short way.
- Linux: the search panel opens in the middle of the screen, and opens again after the window manager closed it.
- Setting the computer's clock back no longer leaves countdowns that never end.
- The menu bar menu follows the language setting; it was always in Chinese.
- An account shortcut pressed before the master password was entered asks for it instead of doing nothing.
- A shortcut the system refused, usually because another app holds it, is no longer shown as working.
- Typing a code from the search panel no longer hides an open main window on macOS, and the panel says so when the
  code was copied instead of typed.
- An import preview left open is forgotten, with its secrets, after 10 minutes or when the main window closes.
- Accounts in the trash for 30 days are deleted even when OTPKeep runs for weeks without a restart.
- Entering the master password or generating a counter code in one window updates the other windows at once.
- Copying the same code twice keeps it on the clipboard for the full time, and a code still waiting to be cleared
  is cleared when OTPKeep quits.
- A rename, edit or counter code made during a sync is no longer lost, and an HOTP counter never goes back.

## Privacy and security

- **Encrypted on your device.** Accounts are stored with XChaCha20-Poly1305; the key lives in the system keychain, or
  is derived from an optional master password with Argon2id.
- **No account, no server, no telemetry.** OTPKeep uses the network only for sync with your own devices nearby while
  a window is open, and for the management page on `127.0.0.1`.
- **Sync you can trust.** The Noise protocol between your devices' Ed25519 identities; the one-time code is checked
  with SPAKE2, so a recorded session cannot be guessed offline.
- **Careful with the clipboard.** Copied codes are kept out of clipboard history apps and cleared after 30 seconds
  (adjustable), only if the clipboard still holds that code.
- **Never reads what is not its own.** OTPKeep never opens keys, passwords or keychain items other than its own.
- **Scripts only with your permission.** The local socket for scripts is in your own data folder, and with a master
  password it stays off until you turn it on.
- **Exports stay private.** An export saved over an existing file is written completely before it replaces that
  file, and is readable only by you even when the old file was readable by others.
- **No private macOS API.** With the quick panel gone, OTPKeep no longer needs it.

## Install

- Script (macOS and Linux, fully automatic): `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/weikxs/otpkeep/main/install.sh | sh`
- Homebrew (macOS): `brew install --cask weikxs/tap/otpkeep`, or `brew upgrade --cask otpkeep`
- A package below; check it against `checksums.txt`

| File | Platform |
|---|---|
| `otpkeep_0.2.1_darwin_universal.dmg` | macOS, Apple silicon and Intel |
| `otpkeep_0.2.1_linux_amd64.deb` / `_arm64.deb` | Debian, Ubuntu, Raspberry Pi OS (x86_64 / arm64) |
| `otpkeep_0.2.1_linux_amd64.rpm` | Fedora, RHEL, openSUSE (x86_64) |
| `otpkeep_0.2.1_linux_amd64.AppImage` / `_arm64.AppImage` | Any Linux with glibc (x86_64 / arm64) |

Then open OTPKeep — it appears in the menu bar (macOS) or the system tray (Linux) — and add your first account.

## Compatibility

- macOS 11 (Big Sur) or newer on Apple silicon and Intel.
- Linux with glibc on x86_64 and arm64: Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora 38+ and their relatives; other
  distributions through the AppImage. Typing codes works on X11, not on Wayland.
- English and Simplified Chinese; other system languages show English.
- Windows, Android and iOS are planned.

## What's coming next

- Windows and Android.

## Notes

- The macOS app is not signed or notarized by Apple; Homebrew and the install script remove the quarantine flag. By
  hand: **Open Anyway** in System Settings → Privacy & Security. See

- There is no v0.2.0 release: that tag stopped before anything was built, when its checks found building the search
  index too slow on slower machines. v0.2.1 has the same changes and builds the index in about half the time.
